newsitem.title: CHINA: China should join WTO but on own terms - Volkswagen.
newsitem.headline: China should join WTO but on own terms - Volkswagen.

text.p: China should join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) but it should not sacrifice its own long-term interests to gain admission now, said Martin Posth, a member of the board of management of Volkswagen AG.
"China's entry into the World Trade Organisation is a must," Posth told an international business conference.
"The entry into the WTO should not mean that China has to ignore its own economic interests," said the executive, who is also chairman of Volkswagen Asia-Pacific Ltd.
"China should instead protect its developing industries... the automotive and its supply industry for a certain period."
Western countries have insisted that China must lower its tariff and non-tariff barriers to trade in order to join the WTO.

Volkswagen, the main producer of cars in China, has been concerned that China might agree to a sharp reduction in tariffs in order to gain entry. Import duties on cars are now about 110 percent of the car's value.
The German automaker builds about 360,000 cars a year at its two joint venture plants in Shanghai and Changchun in the northeast.
Posth has said previously that China needs to protect its car manufacturers and parts suppliers so that they can reach economies of scale that will allow them to compete with foreign manufacturers.
